overview.text: This icon concerns the birth in the flesh of Jesus Christ. Hopko explains the feast as the Son of God becoming human while remaining eternally divine with the Father and the Holy Spirit. The Church’s feast is kept on December 25.

blocks.text: Mary and the swaddled infant occupy the center, with a cave, manger, angels, shepherds, Magi, and Joseph. Some compositions include midwives bathing the Child.
blocks.reason: A necessary concise account of a copyrighted modern publication; no permission to reproduce its full explanation has been established. This is a labelled AI-written summary, not the source author's wording.

blocks.text: Hopko describes a forty-day preparation and a celebration patterned after the Lord’s Resurrection. He explains that Nativity was once celebrated together with Epiphany before receiving its separate date. The services draw together Isaiah’s prophecies, the angelic praise from Luke, Matthew’s account of the Magi, and Paul’s teaching that God sent his Son. These are readings from distinct biblical contexts; the icon brings several parts of the narrative into one composition.

blocks.text: The published explanation makes the subject more than a birthday scene: the one born is the eternal Son, whose becoming human is related to humanity’s salvation and adoption. Hopko points to Galatians 4:4–7 and the feast’s confession of Christ’s divine and human identity.
